title: Changes in Trait Frequency
seo_title: Trait Frequency Worksheets: Allele Frequencies, Survival Rates and Selection (Biology)
standard_text: Apply concepts of statistics and probability to support explanations that organisms with an advantageous heritable trait tend to increase in proportion to organisms lacking this trait.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on changes in trait frequency (NGSS HS-LS4-3): percents, survival rates, allele frequencies and directional, stabilizing and disruptive selection. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Use rates, percents and allele frequencies to show the change.
body_html:
How to think about it

Helpful inherited traits become a bigger share of the population.

  • Use rates and percents, not raw counts, to compare groups.
  • Allele frequency: count alleles. Each AA has 2 A, each Aa has 1 A. p + q = 1.
  • Directional selection shifts the average; stabilizing favors the middle; disruptive favors both ends.
Example

100 plants: 36 AA, 48 Aa, 16 aa. Frequency of A?

A alleles: 72 + 48 = 120

120 ÷ 200

Answer: 0.60

Example

Dark mice: 60 of 100 survived. Light: 40 of 200. Better trait?

60% vs 20%

Answer: dark fur

Common mistakes

  • Counting individuals instead of alleles.
  • Comparing raw counts when the groups are different sizes.
  • Thinking each animal changes during its life.

faq.q: How do you find an allele frequency?
faq.a: Count the copies of the allele (AA has 2, Aa has 1) and divide by the total number of alleles, which is twice the number of individuals.

faq.q: Why compare rates instead of counts?
faq.a: Groups often have different sizes. A rate such as percent surviving gives a fair comparison.

faq.q: What are the three types of selection?
faq.a: Directional selection favors one extreme, stabilizing selection favors the average and disruptive selection favors both extremes.

items.q: If an advantageous trait is inherited, what happens to its proportion over time?
Ben counted 80 snails. 56 of them were striped. What percent were striped?
What is an allele frequency?
c: the fraction of all copies of a gene in a population that are one allele
the number of individuals with a trait

items.q: In a lake, small-beaked and large-beaked birds survive, but medium beaks cannot handle either seed type. Which type of selection is this?
items.e: Both extremes are favored, so the population splits.

items.q: Why do scientists use percentages instead of counts?
c: to compare groups of different sizes

items.q: Chloe counted 500 beetles. 175 of them were green. What percent were green?
Fish with medium body size survive best in a stream with both fast current and predators. Which type of selection is this?
items.e: The middle is favored, so variation shrinks.

items.q: Mia counted 40 crickets. 28 of them were silent. What percent were silent?
In a population with alleles A and a, p is the frequency of A. What is q?
Bacteria exposed to an antibiotic become more resistant each generation. Which type of selection is this?
items.e: One extreme is favored, so the average shifts.

items.q: What does it mean when a population evolves?
c: The frequencies of alleles or traits change over generations.
items.e: Evolution is genetic change in populations.

items.q: What is directional selection?
c: selection that favors one extreme of a trait

items.q: What is stabilizing selection?
c: selection that favors the average trait

items.q: Hunters target the largest elk antlers, and average antler size shrinks. Which type of selection is this?
items.e: One extreme is favored, so the average shifts.

items.q: What is disruptive selection?
c: selection that favors both extremes over the average

items.q: In a population of 40 lizards, 30% are long-legged. How many long-legged lizards are there (Leo's survey)?

items.e: One extreme is favored, so the average shifts.

Salmon: large males fight for mates and tiny males sneak in, but medium males do poorly. Which type of selection is this?
items.e: Both extremes are favored, so the population splits.
